items.text: You must be 19 or older to use, buy, grow or possess cannabis. Adults may carry up to 30 g of dried cannabis (or equivalent) in public, and buy only from the Nova Scotia Liquor Corporation (NSLC), in its stores or online. Cannabis in any form can't be used in a vehicle, by the driver or passengers. Using combustible cannabis in a public place where it's banned can bring a fine of up to C$2,000 (about A$2,033, at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = CAD 0.9838).

The Smoke-free Places Act covers smoking and vaping cannabis as well as tobacco: not on or within 20 m of playgrounds in outdoor public spaces, on or within 9 m of public trails, in provincial parks or on provincial beaches (except inside a rented campsite), on licensed patios, or in a private vehicle with anyone under 19 in it. Municipalities can add their own limits.

From 25 June 2026 fines rose: buying cannabis anywhere other than the NSLC is C$600 to C$5,000 (about A$610 to A$5,082), and a person under 19 found with cannabis faces C$250 to C$500 (about A$254 to A$508).

The legal drinking age is 19; the ticket schedule lists drinking by a person under 19 as its own offence (C$295, about A$300). Being intoxicated in a public place is an offence with a C$134 ticket (about A$136, at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = CAD 0.9838).
